title: Why Do My Pipes Bang or Hammer?

seo.title: Why Do My Pipes Bang or Hammer?
seo.meta_description: Banging pipes can result from water hammer caused by fast valve closure, loose pipes moving, or thermal expansion.
seo.search_intent: Identify the likely causes of “Why Do My Pipes Bang or Hammer?,” use observable clues to choose the first checks, and know when to stop or get professional help.

excerpt: Banging pipes can result from water hammer caused by fast valve closure, loose pipes moving, or thermal expansion. The exact timing—when a faucet closes, a washer valve shuts, or hot piping warms—helps separate the causes.
content_html:
Banging pipes can result from water hammer caused by fast valve closure, loose pipes moving, or thermal expansion. The exact timing—when a faucet closes, a washer valve shuts, or hot piping warms—helps separate the causes.

A bang exactly when flow stops suggests water hammer

Washer and dishwasher solenoid valves close very quickly and can create a pressure wave. If the bang occurs at that instant, an appropriate hammer arrestor or pressure check may help more than randomly fastening pipes.

Banging during warm-up can be thermal expansion

Hot-water pipes expand slightly as they warm and can rub against framing, clamps, or tight penetrations. The noise often develops after hot water begins flowing rather than exactly when a valve closes.

Loose pipes can strike framing

From safe accessible areas, watch whether piping moves when water starts and stops. Use appropriate supports without crushing the pipe or improvising fasteners near electrical wiring.

Excess pressure needs measurement and proper correction

If banging occurs throughout the home, valves fail, or pressure feels unusually high, measure with an appropriate gauge or arrange inspection. Do not randomly adjust a pressure-reducing valve; incorrect settings can create other problems.
